How it plays

Six craft, three minutes, a small arena: the most land when the clock runs out wins. Fly out of your land and your craft draws a line behind it; come back in to claim everything the line encloses. If a rival crosses your line while you are out, it is cut, a spark runs along it and your craft goes up. A destroyed craft comes back in a moment on free ground, not inside anyone's land.

Flying. The craft flies by itself at full speed and never stops. Point the stick where you want to go; let go and it holds its line. After every start it waits for your first touch. BOOST gives a short burst (it recharges). Hold the phone upright or sideways: the game plays both ways.

Pads. Five pads lie on the inner ring, one for each ability, and nothing blocks you: fly straight across them. Hold a pad under your colour to take it: 2 seconds if it is free, 5 to take a rival's (the ring on the pad fills in your colour). Its holder keeps the ability until then and is warned. Be destroyed and you lose your pads at once. A craft holds two pads at most: while you hold two, a free pad under your colour stays free, and a rival's pad you hold for 5 seconds is freed instead of taken.

Missiles two shots: keep a rival in front of you to lock on, then tap. A hit takes half a craft's health: two hits destroy it. A hard turn in its last moment makes a missile miss. Mines three, laid one after another along your path: a mine takes half a craft's health too, so it takes two to destroy one. Shield four seconds: no damage, your line cannot be cut, an EMP does nothing. EMP rivals within 30 m are jammed (no abilities, no boost) and slowed, and their missiles and mines die. Strike lands 1.3 s after you call it, on a rival's line if one is in front of you: it cuts the line, burns the ground for 14 s (land there is lost and cannot be claimed) and hurts craft in it.

Health and repair. Health does not come back by itself. The green pad in the middle is nobody's: fly across it with less than full health and it restores it all, then recharges for 10 seconds. A craft that comes back after being destroyed has full health.

Ramps (a trial; switch them off under Graphics). Three ramps point at the middle. Fly up one and you are in the air for about a second: you cross lines without cutting them, set off no mines, and the line you draw from the air cannot be cut. At full speed you come down on the repair pad; with a boost you fly over it. A clean launch refills your boost.

Land. There are no walls: land is colour, and anyone can cross it. Destroy a rival, by cutting their line or with a weapon, and all their land becomes yours.

Sound

Sound starts with your first touch. In Safari on an iPhone the silent switch mutes it (the TC World app plays through it). M mutes it on a keyboard.

Sun

Afternoon

Keyboard

A and D or the left and right arrows to steer (S or down to ease off), Shift to boost; E missile, Q mines, G shield, V EMP, T strike; C changes the view; M mutes the sound.

  • World Test 13: five abilities on five pads, taken by holding them, two a craft at most; a repair pad (health no longer comes back by itself); a plain colour line for the trail; respawns on free ground; smoother steering; three ramps (a trial); upright and sideways; more announcements. From World Test 12: flat pads, baked colour, relief and roughness textures, a soundtrack, sound effects and an announcer, all made for this game. From World Test 11: hover craft, no barricades, a kill hands you the land. From World Test 10: it flies by itself and you steer. World Test 9's cartoon look: a 240 m arena, toon light and ink outlines; every craft, pad, ramp, plant and cloud is a program written for this game.
  • Rendering: HDR with 4x anti-aliasing, glow, ambient occlusion, depth of field, drifting cloud shadows and a colour grade (High; Medium keeps the glow and the grade; Low is the plain picture).
  • Engine: three.js. Type: Baloo 2 by Ek Type (SIL Open Font License).
